message.content:
You are ADVERSARIALLY VERIFYING one review finding about the repository at
/home/user/adss-2026-09-07, on branch claude/adss-slice-04-revenue-per-order-month.

FINDING: A blank line puts D-0002 outside the deviations register's table, so it does not render as an entry
FILE: /home/user/adss-2026-09-07/docs/deviations.md:20
DETAIL: The register's table runs: header (line 17), delimiter (18), the D-0001 row (19). Line 20 is **blank**, and the D-0002 row is line 21.

In GitHub-flavoured Markdown a blank line terminates a table. D-0001 renders as the table's only row; line 21 renders as a paragraph of literal pipe-separated text with no columns, no header alignment, and no visible field labels — so the "Rule deviated from / Why / Cost / Exit condition / ADR / Status" structure that deviations.md's own "Entry format" section (lines 30-45) says every entry must have is invisible on the rendered page for the entry that has it.

conventions.md §8 covers the shape of these documents ("Prefer a table when there are three or more parallel things to say"; "except table rows, which stay on one line"), and this is the one document whose whole job is to make registered exceptions legible next to each other. Deleting line 20 fixes it.
WHY IT MATTERS: The register is described as "read at the start of every slice" and its value is that entries can be scanned side by side against their exit conditions. A second entry that renders as a wall of pipes is the first step toward exactly what the document warns about: "a year later the rule is folklore." It is also the pattern the next deviation will be appended after.

Your job is to try to DESTROY this finding. Read the actual code. Run the actual command or
test if that settles it. Look for the reason the finding is wrong: a check elsewhere that
already catches it, a documented decision that accepts it on purpose (docs/adr/,
docs/deviations.md, docs/conventions.md, the question documents), an invariant that makes the
bad input impossible, or a simple misreading.

Do NOT modify any file. If you must experiment, copy to a scratch directory.

Return isReal=true ONLY if the defect genuinely exists in this head and is not already
recorded as a known limitation. confidence is 0-10: how sure you are, having tried to break
your own conclusion. If isReal, give the smallest correct fix.

1	# Deviations register
2	
3	Every knowing departure from a principle in [blueprint.md](blueprint.md) or a hard rule in
4	[conventions.md](conventions.md) is recorded here, with the ADR that decided it.
5	
6	The register exists because an unregistered exception is indistinguishable from a mistake. Once
7	one exists, the next person reads it as precedent and copies it, and a year later the rule is
8	folklore. Writing the cost down keeps the trade visible; writing an exit condition down keeps it
9	from becoming permanent by default.
10	
11	A deviation is legitimate only when all four fields are answerable. If the cost cannot be named,
12	the deviation has not been understood. If the exit condition cannot be named, it is not a
13	deviation but a change of rule, and the rule should be superseded instead.
14	
15	## Entries
16	
17	| # | Rule deviated from | Why | Cost | Exit condition | ADR | Status |
18	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
19	| D-0001 | [blueprint.md](blueprint.md) **R2 — No cross-dependency**: "a data product owns its structures and does not consume another product's" | Every slice's page reads one generated Unified Star Schema in `dar__uss`. The structure being shared is additive by construction — keys inherit along many-to-one relationships, measures stay on the stage that owns them — so the fan trap R2 exists to prevent cannot occur **in the measures** — demonstrated in slice 4, the first with two grains: freight is 64,942.69 and revenue 1,265,793.0395 over the whole bridge and per month alike, though 2155 line rows carry an order key. It **can** occur in the peripherals, which is the half this entry asserted too broadly for three slices: a numeric attribute that is also a measure's source is published twice, and `sum(order.freight_charge)` over the bridge returns 207,306.10. ADR 0012 states the rule and refuses a question that breaks it. One shared calendar is what lets two processes be compared at all. Generating a private copy per page would make that comparison a cross-schema join, which is most of what a USS is for | A change made for one reader is visible to all of them the moment it is generated. There is no per-reader projection, so "this reader may not see freight" cannot be expressed. Two readers cannot hold different definitions of the same measure. The first thing to break is a slice needing a measure defined one way for one reader and another way for another — it will have to be modelled as two measures | A second consumer needs isolation: a different shape of the same structure, or a group that must not see part of it. The generator then gains per-group projections over the same bridge and this entry is resolved | [0002](adr/0002-dar-is-one-generated-unified-star-schema.md) | open |
20	
21	| D-0002 | [conventions.md](conventions.md) **§1.1 — DAS keeps the source's words and types**: a contract records what the source sent | The contract vocabulary has `DOUBLE` and `DECIMAL` and no `REAL`, so an `Edm.Single` cannot be recorded faithfully — both options are a choice. `DECIMAL` is chosen because a `NaN` or an `Infinity` then fails at the cast, at `das unpack`, rather than propagating into a measure where both of a question's answers would agree on it and the gate would stay green | A source value with more than the declared scale is refused rather than approximated, which is the right failure and still a failure somebody must handle. And the contract no longer says what the source's metadata says, so a reader comparing the two finds a difference the file does not explain — this entry is that explanation | The contract vocabulary gains a type that is a faithful transcription of a 32-bit float, or the source stops sending one | [0011](adr/0011-a-float-in-the-source-is-recorded-as-a-decimal.md) | open |
22	
23	## Entry format
24	
25	Entries are appended in the order they are decided and never removed. A resolved deviation is
26	marked resolved, with the date and the commit or ADR that resolved it, because the history of why
27	something looked necessary is worth as much as the fact that it no longer is.
28	
29	Field by field:
30	
31	* **Rule deviated from** — quote or link the exact rule. "The spirit of layering" is not a rule;
32	  a row in a blueprint table is.
33	* **Why** — the constraint that made the conforming option unworkable *here*. Convenience, time
34	  pressure and unfamiliarity are not constraints; they are reasons to do it properly.
35	* **Cost** — what this buys the system in trouble. Name the first thing that will break, who pays
36	  for it, and which future change it makes more expensive. A deviation with no cost is evidence
37	  the rule is wrong, so supersede the rule instead of deviating from it.
38	* **Exit condition** — the observable thing that has to become true for the deviation to be
39	  removed. "When we have time" is not observable.
40	* **ADR** — the decision record that argued it. Every deviation has one; the register is the
41	  index, the ADR is the argument.
42	* **Status** — `open` while it stands, `resolved` once it is gone.
43	
44	## Review
45	
46	The register is read at the start of every slice. Each open entry is checked against its exit
47	condition **and against whether its argument is still being carried on assertion**. D-0001 is
48	what that clause was written for. Its justification rests on measures not multiplying across a
49	walk over many-to-one edges; slice 2 built the first edge but both its entities were at one
50	grain, so the walk was exercised and the property was not. Slice 4 brought the second grain and
51	measured it, which is where the argument stopped being carried on assertion — and the same
52	measurement found that the argument was half wrong, which three slices of re-reading the entry
53	had not. That is the clause earning its place: an entry can be true, unexamined, and misleading
54	all at once. An entry should also be re-read the moment a second consumer appears, not only
55	when isolation is demanded, because by then the shared structure will already have shaped both
56	readers. An entry whose exit condition has been met and which is still open is a defect in the
57	same way a failing test is: the system is no longer doing what its own documentation says.

The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## 8. Documentation

| Rule | Why | Severity |
